summary: Forgotten Echoes is a 3D exploration game where students walk the Moon and Mars and uncover the hardware NASA left behind. A scanner and radar show how close a find is without revealing what it is. Players then dig it out and brush the dust off by hand. Each find opens a Catalogue Entry with its mission, year, purpose and current status, plus a short written historical story. Sixteen artifacts are included, three on the Moon (the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, the Apollo 11 Lunar Module descent stage, and the ALSEP science station) and thirteen on Mars (including Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking and Ingenuity). Mars unlocks once the Moon is complete.
details:
What it does. Forgotten Echoes is a 3D exploration game for school-age space fans. You walk the lunar surface and Mars. A scanner and a radar show how close a buried object is, but not what it is. You then dig it out with a short mini-game and brush the dust off by hand with the mouse. Each find opens a Catalogue Entry (mission, year, purpose, current status) and a Journal slot. You can also watch a short written historical story about the hardware. There are 16 artifacts: 3 on the Moon (Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Apollo 11 Lunar Module descent stage, ALSEP) and 13 on Mars (Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking 1 and 2, Phoenix, InSight, Ingenuity, Perseverance hardware and more). Mars unlocks once the Moon is complete.

Benefits and impact. Players learn by finding things, not by reading a list. Each entry separates documented NASA facts (ARCHIVE) from simulated in-game readings (SIM), so students can tell record from simulation. We want players to leave seeing these machines as the work of real people and still-active science.

Tools. Godot 4 with GDScript and the GL Compatibility renderer. IBM Plex fonts, original SVG icons, and a custom “declassified archive” interface design. Artifact text is data-driven (artifacts.json, flashbacks.json) and checked by automated tests.

Creativity. The mystery scanner turns “abandoned equipment” into treasure hunting. The cleaning mini-game reveals each specimen as the player scrubs. The interface looks like a declassified mission file.

Factors considered. Accuracy and source citation, readability at small screen sizes, accessibility (status is never colour alone, reduced-motion option, key hints read from the real controls), and a short, replayable loop.
